narrative:
The model estimates an 88% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook, in order of importance, were your total years of professional experience, whether you had received other job offers, and how long you have been with this current organization.

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (half have only 1–5 years), the model sees your mid-level tenure as aligning more with people who eventually move on. Similarly, the fact that you have received other job opportunities during your time here strongly increased the likelihood of departure; most employees who stay never receive such external offers. Finally, your 1–5 years in this specific role also contributed to the prediction of leaving, as this relatively short tenure at one employer matches the pattern of people who have not yet settled long-term.

Taken together, these signals suggest you may be at a natural transition point. The organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer growth paths, or improved recognition could increase your commitment. You may also wish to reflect on what would make staying worthwhile before deciding on next steps. (248 words)
